items.title: Appending an incomparable tuple does not change the back-and-forth relation of tuples
items.author: David Gonzalez; Dino Rossegger
items.work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 346-349: in the tree of tuples of a structure, for tuples a and b entirely incomparable to a tuple p, appending p to both sides preserves the rank alpha back-and-forth relation in both directions. The statement reduces a comparison of longer tuples to a comparison of shorter ones, and the proof (source lines 350-367) must establish the nontrivial direction of the successor step of a transfinite induction: it splits an arbitrary extension into the part somewhat comparable to p and the part entirely incomparable to it, uses the winning response for the shorter pair, moves that response by an automorphism fixing the first tuple and sending p to an entirely incomparable tuple, and then rearranges the tuples to produce the relation required at the successor rank. What is being compared, and how the incomparability hypothesis is used, is not visible in the statement.
